result.definition: Warranty claims with defect_type "delamination" per 100 decks, counted only among decks that have reached 90 days of field maturity (90 days since ship_date as of the metric's as-of date). Decks younger than 90 days are excluded from both the numerator and the denominator.
result.rationale: Delamination is a defect that surfaces with use, not at the moment of sale — a deck typically has to be ridden, get wet, and take a few impacts before a sub-par adhesive bond starts to show itself. A metric of raw claims over decks shipped is biased toward whichever batches are oldest, because they have had the most time to accumulate claims, and it is biased against the newest batches, which look artificially safe simply because they have not been skated long enough to start to fail. That makes "raw claims over shipped" actively misleading during exactly the window when catching a bad batch matters most: a newly-discovered material problem would look clean under that definition for months, by which time far more decks have shipped. Matching on maturity — comparing batches only once each has had the same amount of field time — is what makes the batches comparable at all, and it is the difference between "we have a lot problem" and "we have a plausible pattern that might just be an aging artifact."
